about: TROMBONE's sprites as the Python kit draws them, RGBA: the instrument inside its glass ball (kit.picture.sprite), the VS card's close-up, and the Pixel Pitch model where the look draws its own

groups.episode: the same call for each of `episode_keys` (what the frames ask for) that `picture` does not already hold
groups.model: sprites.render_sprite(name, radius, yaw, roll): the Pixel Pitch model, for a fighter whose look draws its own sprite
groups.picture: kit.picture.sprite at the four radii, 60 yaws, and each roll in `rolls`
groups.title: title.big_sprite(k), the VS card's close-up

note: Every case is the call on an empty sprite cache. kit.picture.sprite rounds the radius, clips it to 12..30 and rounds the yaw to a multiple of 6 (yk), then calls the look's own sprite(r, float(yk), float(roll)) or, when the look has none, sprites.render_sprite(pp, r, float(yk), float(roll)). Its cache key is "<pp>_<r>_<yk % 360>_<int(roll)>" (`key`): the yaw is wrapped in the key but not in the call, so a look's sprite at yaw -6 and at yaw 354 share a key though they are drawn differently; the first one asked for stays. episode_keys lists (radius, yk, roll) with yk as the frames give it (negative for FLUTE). Arrays are (size, size, 4) uint8: size is 2 * radius + 7 for the model renderer, 2 * radius + 5 for FLUTE's own sprite. A pixel is part of the sprite where alpha > 0.
